draft.title: Community-led change in remote communities
card: Community-led change means a community decides what it needs, plans the program and helps run it. Governments and other groups can support it with funding and skills.
Programs often work better in remote First Nations communities when the community leads them. Local people know their country, culture, needs and priorities.

Locally run health services are one example. They are often run by an Aboriginal community-controlled health organisation. Staff and boards come from the community, so care can fit local culture and language.
Ranger programs are another example. Rangers are paid to care for country, such as managing fire and weeds. They give local jobs and income, and they keep people connected to country and culture.
draft.remember: Programs tend to work better when the community makes the decisions, not when they are only designed for it.

a.q: Why do programs often work better in remote First Nations communities when the community leads them?
opts: Local people know their needs, culture and priorities
Local programs always cost less than outside programs
Governments stop giving funding once a community leads
Outside experts cannot be involved in community programs
a.why: Community leaders know what the community needs and how to reach people, so programs fit local needs and culture. Cost is not the reason given, and support from governments and others can still continue.
a.clue: Think about who knows the community best.

b.q: A remote community in the Northern Territory sets up its own ranger group to manage fire and weeds on its country. Which result shows why community-led change can improve wellbeing?
opts: Local people gain paid jobs and stay connected to country
The community no longer needs any health or school services
Decisions about the program are made by people far away
The program is planned and run only by outside experts
b.why: A ranger group run by the community gives local jobs and income, and it keeps people caring for country. Wellbeing can improve through both. The other options describe outside control, or wrongly say other services are no longer needed.
b.clue: Look for the benefit that stays with local people.

a.best: Local people know their needs, culture and priorities

b.best: Local people gain paid jobs and stay connected to country

problems.detail: The distractor 'Local programs always cost less than outside programs' uses 'always'. The absolute word marks it as wrong without testing the idea, and the card uses 'often' and 'can'.

The distractor 'The program is planned and run only by outside experts' uses 'only', and 'no longer needs any' is also absolute. These words make the wrong options easy to rule out without knowing the idea.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and both questions have one clear right answer. The only issues are minor: absolute words ('always', 'only') in some distractors make them easy to eliminate.

card: Community-led change means a community decides what it needs, plans the program and helps run it. Governments and other groups can support it with funding and skills.

proposal.remember: Programs tend to work better when the community makes the decisions, rather than having them made for it.

a.q: Why do programs often work better in remote First Nations communities when the community leads them?
opts: Local people know their needs, culture and priorities
Outside experts design the program to suit the community
Governments stop giving funding and skills to the program
Decisions are made by officials in the capital cities
a.why: Community leaders know what the community needs and how to reach people, so programs fit local needs and culture. A program designed by outside experts is made for the community, not led by it, and governments can still support community-led programs.
a.clue: Think about who knows the community best.

b.q: A remote community in the Northern Territory sets up its own ranger group to manage fire and weeds on its country. Which result shows why community-led change can improve wellbeing?
opts: Local people gain paid jobs and stay connected to country
Outside experts plan the program and make the decisions
Government support for the area comes to an end
The community relies less on its knowledge of country
b.why: A ranger group run by the community gives local jobs and income, and it keeps people caring for country. Wellbeing can improve through both. Outside experts making the decisions would mean the program is not community-led.
b.clue: Look for the benefit that stays with local people.
